text:
The right pick depends mostly on **how much you need to power** and **how far you carry it**. Here are the strongest options from current 2026 reviews.

## Tent or backpacking-adjacent camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)

The ~250–300Wh class is the sweet spot. These units weigh about 8–10 lb and run a CPAP for 3–5 nights if you turn the humidifier off. [powerstationgearlab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

| Model | Price | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | ~$249 | Lightest at 8.3 lb and very simple to use. Jackery has replaced it with the 300 v2, so it's now sold mainly through Amazon and other retailers. |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | ~$269–299 | Best value. Its 600W inverter is double the Jackery's, and it expands to 572Wh. |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | ~$199 | Built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC version, not the "C300 DC." |
| **Bluetti EB3A** | ~$179 | Cheapest real LiFePO4 option, with a 600W inverter. |

Source: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Its "Check price" buttons lead to the retailers.

## Car camping or running a 12V fridge (~1kWh)

- **Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's "Best Value" pick, currently under $530. It weighs 25 lb and has 6 AC outlets. Its fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: about $799. It's TechRadar's camping pick and PowerStationGearLab's van/overland pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Bluetti AC180**: 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb, $499. A deal site reports that code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off at Bluetti's store as of Oct 21. It can't add expansion batteries. [Buy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate redirect to Bluetti's official US store.

## Long off-grid trips

- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra**: about $1,079. It's WIRED's camping pick: IP65 weatherproof, drop-resistant, and has a one-hand carry handle. It weighs about 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: under $900 on sale and OutdoorGearLab's top-scoring model. It gave 1,710Wh of usable power in testing and weighs 39 lb. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## My quick take
- **Weekend tent camping:** EcoFlow River 3 Plus
- **Car camping with a fridge:** Anker C1000 Gen 2
- **Rugged multi-day trips:** Jackery 1500 Ultra

Black Friday is about a month away, and TechRadar notes it's a good time to watch for price drops. What will you be powering, and for how many nights? I can narrow it down from there.
